{{recipe}}

'''Yassa poulet''' is a popular dish that can be found throughout West Africa, though it specifically originated from Senegal. It has a unique, sweet taste.

== Ingredients ==

* 6 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] thighs
* 3 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, neatly [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|dijon mustard]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|smoked paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon powder]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==

# Wash the chicken and pat it dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
# Put the chicken in a large bowl with the garlic, onions, dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt, bouillon powder, cayenne pepper and smoked paprika. Mix together well and place in the fridge to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] for 2–12 hours.
# Take the chicken out of the marinade, and scrape off the marinade and the onions. Reserve the marinade.
# Heat the olive oil in the large [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]] over medium heat, and add the chicken. Let it brown on both sides for 5 minutes. Take out and set aside the chicken.
# To the pot, add the onions and remaining marinade. Cook on medium heat for 5 minutes until browned.
# Return the browned chicken pieces to the sweet caramelized onions.
# Add the chicken broth, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 20 minutes over medium heat until the chicken is fully cooked.
# Taste for salt and other ingredients and make any necessary adjustments.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you cannot eat it all at once, you can store it in the fridge for four days and in the deep freezer for up to 6 months.
* You can reheat this dish in a skillet over medium heat—if you notice it is too dry you can add a splash of chicken broth to make it moist.
* Try using a different type of [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] like whole grain or spicy brown if Dijon is not readily available.
* You can adjust the spice level to your taste. You can add some extra spice such as [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to improve its flavour.
* Try to brown the chicken well, as this improve the look and flavor.
* Make sure you use fresh lemon to get a nice taste—if this is not available, you can make use of bottled lemon or lime juice.
* It can be eaten with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:Cauliflower Rice|cauliflower rice]].
